sections.heading: Pros
sections.text:
Top-tier damage ceiling with a focus on mid-air combat and animations that are generally hard to interrupt.

 Excels in all endgame content, not just single-target bossing - Havoc Bane is applied by herself very often and constantly spreads across multiple waves.

 Energy Regen requirements are super easy to meet.

 Has a ton of accessible team compositions, F2P and Premium alike. F2P-friendly while also being improvable for cheap, likely some of her premium characters are already present on your account as well.

 Has a short rotation compared to most Main DPS while still dealing ludicrous damage.

 Looks like Selena from Punishing: Gray Raven (we like Selena from Punishing: Gray Raven).

sections.heading: Cons
sections.text:
Self-buffs CRIT stats by so much that Shorekeeper is rendered practically useless; she is hence more limited in premium 3rd slot options than most (Mornye only with Lynae, or Chisa are your only upgrade paths from Verina).

 Somewhat limited in Swap Cancelling; currently plays best with Outro buffers, her damage is spread evenly across her rotation, preventing buffing key abilities, and a lot of her self-buffs only apply if she’s the active character on the field.

sections.heading: Review
sections.text: Yangyang: Xuanling (who we will just shorten to YY:XL throughout this review) is a 5-star Havoc Sword Main DPS character who relies on Havoc Bane and Heavy Attack damage to execute pretty fast & most importantly really strong rotations that will, with enough investment, decimate her enemies, as she is one of the top DPS characters in the game by a landslide.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics & Rotation
sections.text:
YY:XL applies Havoc Bane constantly with most of the attacks in her rotation, upkeeping max stacks on all enemies at all times (even in multi-wave content) is something she can handle easily. Havoc Bane constantly applies DEF Shred to affected enemies, as well as Havoc DMG Amplification to Yangyang via one of her passives (up to 6 stacks).
 Her rotation relies on switching between Azure and Feather stance. By default, she starts her rotations in Azure stance. She can switch freely between both forms via her Skill, however she can do so using enhanced skills if her Melody Forte gauge is depleted fully (via Perfect Dodges or Basic Attacks). This restores her other Forte resource, Azure Plume, which enhances her Mid-Air Attack and Azure Heavy Attack. In short, her rotation has her consuming her melody bar once, switching between both of her forms and casting her key attacks consecutively until she switches out.
 YY:XL additionally self-buffs her CRIT DMG throughout her rotation, as executing it will enhance the CRIT DMG of her key attacks by massive amounts (she reaches above 500% total CRIT DMG with a standard build and team, which leads to as bonkers of a damage ceiling as you’d expect).
 Finally, her Outro buffs the Havoc DMG of other Havoc Bane appliers than herself in the team on top of dealing a small amount of damage (right now, only Chisa can use this).
 YY:XL’s kit is very wordy but boils down to the self-buffs we detailed above, as well as ensuring that Havoc Bane is constantly applied on enemies up to max stacks at all times, even in multi-wave content, so that’s really all we have to say on her kit before we conclude.

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
sections.text:
In the meta, YY:XL is a pretty imposing presence, to say the least. The nature of her kit makes her excel in all situations - AoE, single-target, single-wave, multi-wave, F2P or premium; you name it - she does it. In spite of her Signature weapon granting her a good increase over Emerald of Genesis, she still winds up one of the most F2P-friendly characters in the game, thanks to one of her best supports, Rebecca, being free, as well as her base damage simply being super high.
 Her ability to work with proven AoE powerhouses like Phrolova, and generally applicable as well as accessible Supports like Lynae, Rebecca or even Mortefi, makes her a powerhouse with extremely few flaws, that we honestly had trouble coming up with during this review (finding cons to YY:XL’s pros is genuinely a difficult task). Overall, she is one of the most meta releases, if not the most meta DPS to ever release. F2P-friendly, and one of the highest ceilings for scoring across all endgames. Those 2 combined traits are simply things we have never seen before. Luuk got close, but struggles hard in Whimpering Wastes. YY:XL doesn’t.
 In conclusion, YY:XL is one of the best DPS characters in Wuthering Waves overall. She only has room to grow post-release thanks to her ability to benefit from a wide variety of buffs paired alongside a ridiculously high base level of damage. Definitely one of the most imposing meta releases to date, YY:XL basically cannot disappoint on practically any Wuthering Waves account. If you were hesitant to pick her up and the determining factor was her meta position, rest assured - she’s top tier, no doubt.

YY:XL applies Havoc Bane constantly with most of the attacks in her rotation, upkeeping max stacks on all enemies at all times (even in multi-wave content) is something she can handle easily. This restores her other Forte resource, Azure Plume, which enhances her Mid-Air Attack and Azure Heavy Attack. In short, her rotation has her consuming her melody bar once, switching between both of her forms and casting her key attacks consecutively until she switches out.
 YY:XL additionally self-buffs her CRIT DMG throughout her rotation, as executing it will enhance the CRIT DMG of her key attacks by massive amounts (she reaches above 500% total CRIT DMG with a standard build and team, which leads to as bonkers of a damage ceiling as you’d expect).
 Finally, her Outro buffs the Havoc DMG of other Havoc Bane appliers than herself in the team on top of dealing a small amount of damage (right now, only Chisa can use this).
 YY:XL’s kit is very wordy but boils down to the self-buffs we detailed above, as well as ensuring that Havoc Bane is constantly applied on enemies up to max stacks at all times, even in multi-wave content, so that’s really all we have to say on her kit before we conclude.

 Her rotation relies on switching between Azure and Feather stance. By default, she starts her rotations in Azure stance. She can switch freely between both forms via her Skill, however she can do so using enhanced skills if her Melody Forte gauge is depleted fully (via Perfect Dodges or Basic Attacks). This restores her other Forte resource, Azure Plume, which enhances her Mid-Air Attack and Azure Heavy Attack. In short, her rotation has her consuming her melody bar once, switching between both of her forms and casting her key attacks consecutively until she switches out.
 YY:XL additionally self-buffs her CRIT DMG throughout her rotation, as executing it will enhance the CRIT DMG of her key attacks by massive amounts (she reaches above 500% total CRIT DMG with a standard build and team, which leads to as bonkers of a damage ceiling as you’d expect).
 Finally, her Outro buffs the Havoc DMG of other Havoc Bane appliers than herself in the team on top of dealing a small amount of damage (right now, only Chisa can use this).
 YY:XL’s kit is very wordy but boils down to the self-buffs we detailed above, as well as ensuring that Havoc Bane is constantly applied on enemies up to max stacks at all times, even in multi-wave content, so that’s really all we have to say on her kit before we conclude.
 Meta Position & Conclusion
 In the meta, YY:XL is a pretty imposing presence, to say the least. The nature of her kit makes her excel in all situations - AoE, single-target, single-wave, multi-wave, F2P or premium; you name it - she does it. In spite of her Signature weapon granting her a good increase over Emerald of Genesis, she still winds up one of the most F2P-friendly characters in the game, thanks to one of her best supports, Rebecca, being free, as well as her base damage simply being super high.
 Her ability to work with proven AoE powerhouses like Phrolova, and generally applicable as well as accessible Supports like Lynae, Rebecca or even Mortefi, makes her a powerhouse with extremely few flaws, that we honestly had trouble coming up with during this review (finding cons to YY:XL’s pros is genuinely a difficult task). Overall, she is one of the most meta releases, if not the most meta DPS to ever release. F2P-friendly, and one of the highest ceilings for scoring across all endgames. Those 2 combined traits are simply things we have never seen before. Luuk got close, but struggles hard in Whimpering Wastes. YY:XL doesn’t.
 In conclusion, YY:XL is one of the best DPS characters in Wuthering Waves overall. She only has room to grow post-release thanks to her ability to benefit from a wide variety of buffs paired alongside a ridiculously high base level of damage. Definitely one of the most imposing meta releases to date, YY:XL basically cannot disappoint on practically any Wuthering Waves account. If you were hesitant to pick her up and the determining factor was her meta position, rest assured - she’s top tier, no doubt.
